criteria.rationale: The deciding metric, contribution margin per order, is negative on the data shown, and customer loyalty is unproven.

evidence.text: Contribution margin negative on the data shown; customer loyalty unproven.

evidence.text: Operational knowledge real and detailed: picking times, rider utilisation, wastage by category.

criteria.rationale: A me-too in a hot, crowded category with deep-pocketed incumbents; local ambition (one neighbourhood cluster).

evidence.text: Under-ten-minute delivery from dark stores in one neighbourhood cluster.

case_for: Founders with detailed, hands-on quick-commerce operating knowledge and a live cluster (R2, S3).
Energetic team at a stage the fund can lead (S2).
case_against: Profitability at density is delegated to a future large raise (R1, R5).
Me-too in a hot category against deep-pocketed incumbents (S4, R4, R6).
call_questions: At what order density does a single dark store reach positive contribution margin, and how far are you from it today?
What is 30/90-day retention in your cluster, and what share of orders come from discounts?
Is there a niche (category, geography, customer) where you can be profitable without matching incumbents' spend?
What do you do if the large raise you need never comes?
Incumbents already run your exact playbook with far more capital - tell us why we're wrong to see this as a me-too.
what_would_change_our_view: Positive contribution margin in the existing cluster, or a defensible niche where the model works without a large raise to reach density.
